examples.text: We never say 12 a.m. or 12 p.m. It's either 12 midnight or 12 noon, respectively.
The 12-hour clock uses A.M. for the morning hours of midnight (12:00 A.M.) to almost noon (11:59 A.M.) and the P.M. designation for the hours from noon (12:00 P.M.) to almost midnight (11:59 PM).
examples.ref: 2009, Robert Bill, Medical Mathematics and Dosage Calculations for Veterinary Professionals, page 348:

examples.text: The 12-hour clock, which is used in the U.S., Canada, and a few other countries, divides time into two cycles: a.m. (ante meridiem, Latin for before midday) from midnight, 12 a.m., to 11:59 a.m.; and p.m. (post meridiem, Latin for after midday) from noon, 12 p.m., to 11:59 p.m.
